A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reason50K dataset and ReasonBrain framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative editing results in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations and evaluations of efficiency, human preferences, multi-step editing, identity preservation, and data construction.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds SID-inspired context/instruction-aware token selection and TAME-based dynamic token propagation to the stated MLLM training procedure. The main FRCE/CME architecture, guidance-generation procedure, and losses remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The five benchmark datasets and four Reason50K reasoning categories are retained. Appendix F adds two-step and three-step sequential editing scenarios, extending task requirements beyond the original single-step evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: the six baselines in Table 2, the additional Emu Edit comparator in Table 3, and ChatGPT-4o in qualitative comparisons. New appendix comparisons reuse existing baselines; SID and TAME are cited training techniques, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation settings for a 3B model, inference timing, multi-step editing, identity preservation, data-generation controls, and multiple training targets. It also introduces a randomized preference study with 50 images and 30 participants. The original splits and main hyperparameters remain unchanged; Appendix E corrects the annotation-dataset description from ReasonEdit++ to Reason50K without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds four individual component-removal conditions beyond v1's cumulative ablations. Appendix F adds analyses of model size, sequential-edit stability, defective data-generation stages, unidirectional versus full CME interaction, identity preservation, and one-to-many target mappings. The reorganized qualitative appendix figures reuse existing cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging ten annotators' alignment ratings is retained. The new preference study changes evaluation sampling but introduces no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3, Figure 5, and the original Table 4 rows retain their results. New entries include component-removal scores and the appendix evaluations: Table A2 reports 24-second inference for the 3B variant versus 32 seconds for 7B, while Table A4 reports ReasonBrain preferences of 75.71% for instruction alignment and 63.55% for image quality. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the token-prediction and diffusion objectives (A1)–(A2), and their mathematical definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central dataset, reasoning-module, performance, and generalization claims. The introduction newly claims that joint reasoning and editing avoids multi-round textual refinement and reduces reasoning uncertainty and inference time.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning synthetic data and transfer to real-world video conditions. Appendix F attributes multi-step stability to the ID Controller, multiple-target degradation to conflicting optimization signals, and data-quality effects to particular construction stages. It also newly interprets identity-preservation results as excluding shortcut learning, a stronger inference than those scores alone establish.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly identifies Video-LLaVA as the evaluator and documents its inputs, binary judging prompt, and score aggregation, although the prompt contains '[object Object]' placeholders. Appendix A specifies code release after acceptance. Previously reported training hyperparameters, hardware, and the repository address are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SID, TAME, GPT-Image-Edit-1.5M, and Complex-Edit for training, dataset limitations, and identity evaluation. It also adds an explicit efficiency distinction from MGIE-style textual refinement. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained with limited editing and explanatory additions. Experimental setups move from Section 4.1 to Appendix E, appendices are reorganized, citations switch to author-year style, and Xueqin Chen's affiliation changes from TU Delft to Sichuan University. There is no extensive rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 4 and adds eight appendix tables. The original two qualitative appendix grids are split and transposed into four larger figures, A2–A5, making the same examples and labels easier to inspect. The document template and figure placement also change, while the main figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's cumulative ablations, v2's individual component removals strengthen attribution, while data-construction tests, explicit synthetic-data limitations, and clearer appendix figures improve assessment and transparency. These gains are moderated by ambiguous new protocols, including three requested human selections but only two defined criteria, and the unsupported inference that identity preservation excludes shortcut learning. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
